passes.name: Skill Check authoring and assessment coverage

findings.message: The withdrawn CPPL Revision 1 artifact remains preserved for comparison and is not a learner-catalog entry.
External resource access and exact consumption boundaries must be rechecked before a future curriculum revision.

semanticValidation.method: Human-led adversarial review examined the complete-beginner target, all 25 competencies and 34 concepts, every weekly Study assignment and source-mapped question, eight Build contracts, prerequisite edges, modern C++ ownership and failure boundaries, session limits, and human-review Proof. Deterministic validation consumes this judgment but does not manufacture it.
findingsReviewed: Rejected Revision 1's repeated generated concept-card route and required bounded, inspected external teaching plus prediction, compilation, tracing, debugging, or verification before each Skill Check.

Kept Week 1 deliberately gentle: a supplied banner scaffold, fixed initialized values, output, compilation, execution, one compile-stopping error, and one genuine warning under the stated flags; there is no input, decision, loop, collection, class, or calculator.

Standardized beginner input on getline plus a supplied istringstream full-parse helper, avoiding the formatted-input/newline trap, prefix-accepting conversions, and unexplained exception-based parsing.

Used std::string, std::vector, value returns, const references, private class state, standard algorithms, std::map, and scoped streams as the main path; raw arrays, new/delete, pointer ownership, and manual cleanup are outside this course.

Bounded Week 5 exceptions to one inspected throw/try/catch lesson, a visible scaffold, four named construction/transition failures, and pre-mutation checks while keeping inheritance, custom destructors, and raw pointers out.
Made iterator end checks, value capture, source-backed strict comparator rules, copied sorting, pre-sized transform output, and non-inserting map lookup observable before assessing them.

Supplied exact file fixtures and a std::error_code filesystem helper; learner code completes and checks the candidate before promotion, retains .bak until success, handles rollback results, and proves no mutation on malformed or failed storage paths.
Used dependency-free C++ check functions so verification adds no package manager, test framework, account, or network prerequisite.

Required every graded item to map to an inspected resource assigned in the same Week, cover a distinct learning target, use one defensible answer and C++-specific distractors, distribute authored positions, and retain runtime option reshuffling.

Kept every Build session between 60 and 105 minutes, below the two-hour cap; setup remains separate and capability-skippable, and Week 8 integrates established behavior instead of introducing a second technology stack.
semanticValidation.adversarialResult: PASS after the recorded repairs. The course teaches modern standard-library C++ value ownership and RAII rather than translating the C course or introducing raw-memory mechanics. The .tmp/.bak protocol is explicitly a bounded instructional recovery contract, not a claim of universal transactional durability. No required Build depends on an unresolved competency.
